_doc: Committed recipe for the REPEATABLE painterly backdrop workflow (generate_room.py). The renderer/registry consume the GENERATED plate; this file is the source of truth for HOW a plate is generated, so any room is regeneratable on demand. Proven 2026-06-30: the crypt base plate (flat museum-lit, lighting 5/10, L6 6) re-lit via this img2img recipe into firelit chiaroscuro. Pipeline = Scenario img2img on model_z-image + our painterly LoRA. The lever from 6.5->8 is LIGHTING DRAMA, not more texture (drop ambient, single warm key, deep blue-violet shadows, hard cast shadows). Composition is camera-pinned and must NOT drift: strength stays low (~0.45) so the dimetric layout (pillars/sarcophagus/brazier/walls) holds while diffusion re-lights.

_outdoor_lighting_note_2026_07_08: backdrop-cadence restart (HV5, #1386): TWO new lighting siblings for OPEN-AIR rooms — daylight_outdoor (day) and firelit_outdoor (night) — because the existing firelit/daylight templates are INTERIOR-specific ('back and side walls', 'tall windows', 'stained-glass shaft'), wrong for an exterior plate (camp_clearing_night, market_square). Wired via generate_room.py --lighting {daylight_outdoor|firelit_outdoor} (each falls back to its interior sibling if the manifest lacks the key, so older manifests keep working). --day --lighting daylight_outdoor keeps the outdoor template for pass1 while still routing pass2/pass3 through the existing day-state layered pipeline (layered_pipeline_day_2026_07_03) — see generate_room.py's --day guard. firelit_outdoor has no --day interaction (it IS the night state).
multipass_note: Best result = base plate -> pass1 relight (strength 0.45) -> pass2 deep-shadow refine (strength 0.30, same prompt). Each pass low-strength to protect the camera-pinned composition (L1). generate_room.py --refine-from <asset_id> chains a pass.
ceiling_2026_06_30: This pipeline tops out ~7.4/10 backdrop (crypt: lighting/registration/detail/washout all solved, L1=8). The L6>=8 BINDING gate is NOT cleared: PoE2-grade CARVED-STONE micro-craft (fluted pillars, chiseled relief, masonry coursing, sculpted sarcophagus) is beyond what this painterly LoRA + img2img renders from a SMOOTH-PRIMITIVE greybox. THE LEVER TO >=8: a greybox with carved geometry (so img2img has carved structure to preserve), or a crisper architectural model/LoRA. Tracked as the M-A->>=8 follow-up; the 7.4 firelit plate is adopted for the demo (the plate is swappable later with zero renderer/actor rework).
textured_greybox_result_2026_07_01: The carved-GEOMETRY greybox lever (build_room_greybox.cs) was driven to its empirical ceiling via a SCORED loop (qa/scores_db surface=visual, harsh PoE2 panel). A flat gray greybox img2img's to ~4.75. Adding, in order: (1) a procedural STONE ALBEDO+NORMAL (textured base, not flat grey) -> 5.75; (2) LIT walls (strong cool fill so the carved walls don't crush to black) -> 6.5; (3) GEOMETRIC masonry coursing on the wall faces (the floor painted into flagstones because it has geometric grout boxes; the walls needed the same) -> 7.07. DENSER coursing yielded NO gain (~6.8, within variance). CONCLUSION (confirms the line above): geometry tops out ~7.07 — the LoRA paints FOCAL craft (floor flagstones, statue niches, fluted columns, figural relief panels) at genuine PoE2-grade but SMOOTHS the broad wall FIELDS into 'value-pass', regardless of coursing density. >=8 is LoRA-BOUND, not geometry-bound: needs a crisper architectural/stone LoRA (or a dedicated detail pass on the broad wall fields). KEY WIN: this 7.07 is reached at LOW img2img strength (0.5-0.52) which PRESERVES the camera-pin -> the painted props stay on the authored-pathing cells (the firelit 7.4 plate had hand-tuned obstacles; this is authored-pathing-aligned AND repeatable from any scene_grid). Plate: renders/crypt14_walledcourse_v1.png; live combat: m1_combat_textured.png; progression: LEVER_progression_6up.png.

seedream_v2_2026_07_01: TESTED + SCORED, NOT ADOPTED (an earlier version of this note over-claimed a '≥8 BREAKTHROUGH' off ONE eyeballed crypt render — that claim is REFUTED). Seedream 4.5 (seedream_model) is a modern structure-preserving img2img EDITOR: swap it in for model_z-image+painterly-LoRA and it holds the camera-pin well (aspectRatio:auto; solid obstacles stay on their pathing cells; ambiguous props like a lava-box may be reinterpreted). Fast ~30s / ~6 CU. BUT the rigorous visual-critic panel (3 independent harsh PoE2-anchored scorers/image) scored: crypt (renders/seedream_crypt_v2.png) = 4.0, hell (renders/seedream_hell_test.png) = 5.0 — BOTH below-bar, and NOT better than the OLD LoRA firelit crypt which scores 4.7 on the SAME panel (its '7.4' was also inflated). So Seedream is NOT a ≥8 unlock and is NOT adopted; the pipeline default stays model_z-image+LoRA. ≥8 remains OPEN. REPRODUCED blockers across ALL current pipelines (the real levers): (a) WASHOUT/flat value — floor sits in a narrow value band, shadows are a flat uniform tint not integrated painted light, no deep-shadow anchors/dramatic chiaroscuro; (b) REPETITION — cloned wall tiles + cloned props; (c) SPARSE/generic asset-kit composition — few props, dead floor, no environmental storytelling. Call kept for reference: model_run(seedream_model, referenceImages=[<uploaded greybox asset_id>], prompt=<biome sentence> + ' ' + poe2_refined_prompt_suffix, size='2K', aspectRatio='auto'). LESSON: SCORE every candidate with the ≥2-run panel BEFORE claiming a bar or swapping a workflow.
gemini_polish_populate_pass_2026_07_01: ★ BEST REPEATABLE ≥8-DIRECTION LEVER FOUND (4 anchored scored panels; still a ~6.0-6.5 ceiling, NOT >=8, but a ROBUST +0.4-0.9 gain). After a painterly base plate exists (img2img OR the G-buffer relight pipeline), run ONE Gemini-3.1 instruction-edit 'polish + POPULATE' pass. It is an instruction editor (model_google-gemini-3-1-flash, referenceImages=[<base asset_id>], resolution '2K', thinkingLevel 'HIGH', aspectRatio 'auto', numOutputs 2 — NO strength knob, so preservation is prompt-driven). ONE pass does five things: (1) re-carve the FOCAL sculpture (e.g. sarcophagus effigy) into crisp readable detail (fixes 'melted mush'); (2) DE-CLONE repeated props — 'make the two columns DISTINCT, each a unique capital + relief' (fixes the diffusion repetition tell); (3) PAINT any flat-gray greybox faces the strict-preserve pass left unpainted (e.g. column top-caps); (4) ADD pathing-safe environmental-storytelling clutter ONLY along walls/corners/edges keeping the central combat floor CLEAR (bones/skull, fallen sword+shield, cobwebs, a wall torch-bracket, toppled urn+coins, leaves, moss) — this is the biggest lever, it lifts the COMPOSITION lens ~4.5->6.2 (attacks the 'empty asset-showcase diorama' flaw the panel weights hardest); (5) deepen the void openings toward true-black. SCORED (anchored panel, 5 harsh PoE2 scorers, a FIXED in-panel anchor per feedback_visual_panel_scoring_variance): density crypt = 6.2 vs anchor 5.3 (+0.9) vs pre-polish baseline 5.8 (+0.4). Best crypt plate to date -> box Assets/painterly/backdrops/crypt_dense_v1.png. REMAINING gap to >=8 (measured, consistent): (a) monochromatic warm palette, NO cool counter-light (~95% hues in orange bins — an in-engine relight cool-fill is the Phase-C fix); (b) carved detail still slightly 'mushy up close' (LoRA/model-bound); (c) 'flat illustration vs lit-3D-render' medium gap. ADOPT this pass; the real >=8 bet beyond it is a CLEAN char-free architectural LoRA. Full campaign log: ~/worldos-session-notes/2026-07-01-ge8-diffuse-campaign/implementation-notes.md.
poe2_refined_prompt_suffix: Keep the EXACT same layout, geometry, props, and camera angle. Crisp chiseled carved-stone detail, sharp architectural relief and clean mortar lines. Warm firelit key light with deep cool blue-violet shadows, dramatic atmospheric chiaroscuro, Pillars of Eternity 2 pre-rendered isometric game background. Clean REFINED digital matte painting, game-ready background art — NOT thick impasto oil paint, NO visible canvas texture, NO painting border or frame, full-bleed edge to edge. No characters, no text.
_prompt_ab_2026_07_03: ADOPTED. Prompt A/B (panel9, 5 scorers, control-anchored, same incumbent LoRA + same crypt greybox @ strength 0.55): the STAGING-LAW prompt variant beat the prior firelit_positive_template 5/5 scorers, +0.7 median (5.5 vs 4.8) — unanimous direction at the noise threshold, zero-cost reversible string swap. Delta folded into firelit_positive_template above: 'loose confident visible oil-paint brushstrokes', 'varied unique pillar carvings, no two columns identical', 'crisply chiseled stone relief', 'environmental storytelling clutter along the walls'; washout_negative gained 'identical cloned columns, repeating tiled pattern'. Tested on the crypt room but the added language is room-agnostic (no crypt-specific nouns) and applies to every room via the shared template. Both arms of the A/B confirm composition/craft comes from the LAYERED passes (see layered_pipeline_2026_07_02), not pass-1 alone — this is a pass-1 quality-of-base-plate improvement, not a substitute for layering. Evidence: ~/worldos-session-notes/2026-07-03-prompt-ab/ (panel9).

layered_pipeline_2026_07_02._doc: ADOPTION-GRADE 3-pass LAYERED recipe, validated 2026-07-02 on a full multi-room plate (2-panel evidence, 5 scorers, control-anchored). ORDER LAW (do not reorder): pass1 LAYOUT (macro img2img) -> pass2 DETAIL/POPULATE (Gemini instruction-edit) -> pass3 STAGING LAST (Gemini instruction-edit). The detail/populate pass flattens lighting while it re-carves/de-clones/populates; the staging pass restores dramatic chiaroscuro lighting WITHOUT losing the detail pass's gains — running staging before detail loses the order-law benefit. Scored progression: pass1 base v4-LoRA img2img 6.0 -> +pass2 detail/populate 6.3-7.2 -> +pass3 staging 7.6 median. Production anchor (same panel) = 8.4. Evidence: ~/worldos-session-notes/2026-07-02-lora-v4-eval/ (panel4 = pre-staging delta, panel5 = full 3-pass delta; panel23_results.json + mapping4/5_DO_NOT_STAGE.txt carry the per-scorer numbers). Wired via generate_room.py --layered (default OFF; no flag = byte-identical single-pass behavior).

pass1_layout._doc: Existing img2img macro pass — UNCHANGED from the single-pass recipe above (base_model + lora + defaults). LoRA choice is the existing recipe's default, not a layered-pipeline-specific change.
pass1_layout._lora_note: The incumbent painterly LoRA (model_MB22WaRCBLtfhi5R2CRpHoEL, room_recipes.json top-level `lora`) remains the generate_room.py DEFAULT — it beat worldos-poe2-clean-env-v4 head-to-head (see CANONICAL.md ≥8 row, 2026-07-02 RESOLVED). worldos-poe2-clean-env-v4 (model_ng6MSaWtyvwKbZyDBMtzv7tA) is kept ONLY as an optional dark-staging txt2img/img2img alternative lane (it natively generates the PoE staging-law near-black value structure) — not a default swap.
pass1_layout.strength_contract: strength stays the camera-pin knob: 0.5-0.6 for the standard authored-pathing contract, 0.75 for a hero/supersampled macro pass. Low strength protects the camera-pinned composition; this knob is UNCHANGED by layering the two detail passes on top.

pass2_detail_populate._doc: Gemini instruction-edit detail/populate pass. Runs AFTER pass1, on pass1's output asset. TEMPLATIZED 2026-07-03 (fix for the tavern-turned-crypt defect: this prompt was previously hardcoded with crypt nouns and applied unconditionally to every room by generate_room.py --layered, silently repainting a tavern base plate into a crypt). Slots are filled per-room from room_recipes.json:rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots. The crypt slot values were chosen so the RENDERED template is byte-identical to the prior hardcoded crypt prompt (regression-guarded by a unit test).
pass2_detail_populate.prompt_template: Edit this painterly isometric {room_setting_noun} plate. PRESERVE the exact composition, camera, room layout, and the dark dramatic lighting with its warm fire pools and deep shadows — do not brighten the scene. IMPROVE only the craft: re-sculpt every {room_focal_features} so they read CRISPLY CHISELED with clean edge highlights; make every {room_repeat_elements} UNIQUE (remove cloned repeats); paint any flat gray or unfinished surfaces as weathered stone; add small environmental-storytelling clutter along walls and edges only ({room_clutter_vocab}) keeping the open floor areas clear; deepen the black voids at the openings. Keep the hand-painted oil-paint brushwork feel throughout. Do NOT add any text, letters, numbers, runic writing that reads as text, labels, legends, map insets, UI elements, frames, or borders — the plate must contain ONLY the diegetic painted scene. Do NOT add any characters, people, figures, animals, or creatures of any kind — this is an EMPTY background plate; actors are composited in separately by the engine.
pass2_detail_populate.prompt_template_note: slots: room_setting_noun (e.g. 'dungeon'/'tavern'/'cathedral'), room_focal_features (the crisp-carve target nouns), room_repeat_elements (the de-clone target nouns), room_clutter_vocab (comma list of wall/edge clutter items). Filled per-room from rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots by generate_room.py; crypt's slot values reproduce the prior hardcoded prompt byte-for-byte.

pass3_staging_last._doc: Gemini instruction-edit STAGING pass. Runs LAST, on pass2's output asset — this order is the load-bearing finding: staging must come after detail/populate, not before, because the detail pass flattens lighting and the staging pass restores it without erasing the detail gains. TEMPLATIZED 2026-07-03 (fix for the tavern-turned-crypt defect: this prompt was previously hardcoded with crypt light-source/space nouns and applied unconditionally to every room). Slots filled per-room from rooms.<room>.layered.pass3_slots; the crypt slot values reproduce the prior hardcoded crypt prompt byte-for-byte (regression-guarded by a unit test).
pass3_staging_last.prompt_template: Edit this painterly isometric {room_setting_noun} plate. PRESERVE every detail exactly — the room layout, all {room_preserve_list} — change NOTHING about the content or composition. ONLY restage the LIGHTING into dramatic chiaroscuro: make {room_key_source} the dominant warm key light with a bright hot pool around it, let {room_fill_source} each cast a small local warm pool with HARD directional cast shadows from the pillars and props, and sink everything between the pools into deep cool blue-violet shadow — corners, far rooms, and floors away from lights should fall near-black. Steep warm-to-cool falloff, warm rim light on edges facing flames, cool bounce on shadow-side stone. The scene must read as small pools of firelight in {room_space_desc}, keeping the hand-painted oil feel. Do NOT add any text, letters, numbers, runic writing that reads as text, labels, legends, map insets, UI elements, frames, or borders — the plate must contain ONLY the diegetic painted scene. Do NOT add any characters, people, figures, animals, or creatures of any kind — this is an EMPTY background plate; actors are composited in separately by the engine.
pass3_staging_last.prompt_template_note: slots: room_setting_noun, room_preserve_list (comma list of props/features to hold fixed), room_key_source (the dominant warm light noun phrase), room_fill_source (the secondary local-pool light noun phrase), room_space_desc (e.g. 'a vast dark crypt'). Filled per-room from rooms.<room>.layered.pass3_slots by generate_room.py.

layered_pipeline_2026_07_02.downscale_note: If the Gemini 2K output exceeds the plate size (1344x768 contract), downscale with PIL LANCZOS to match — see generate_room.py --layered.
layered_pipeline_2026_07_02.sequencing_note: Sequential jobs only (Scenario rule — concurrent paints collide/silently no-output). Each pass waits on the prior pass's terminal job status before submitting.
layered_pipeline_2026_07_02._hallucination_note: 2026-07-02 church-run incident: the pass2 Gemini detail/populate pass HALLUCINATED a map inset + garbled legend text onto the church plate (3/5 panel scorers called it an unshippable production artifact). Root cause: Gemini instruction-edit models have no strength knob and will sometimes invent UI-chrome-like elements (insets, legends, labels) when asked to 'add environmental-storytelling detail'. Fix: both pass2_detail_populate.prompt and pass3_staging_last.prompt now end with an explicit hard negative sentence forbidding text/labels/legends/map-insets/UI-elements/frames/borders. Evidence: ~/worldos-session-notes/2026-07-02-lora-v4-eval/.

layered_pipeline_day_2026_07_03._doc: DAY-STATE variant of layered_pipeline_2026_07_02, for issue #1291 day/night live integration (G5a — the GENERATION half; box wiring is a separate later unit). Same ORDER LAW (pass1 layout -> pass2 detail/populate -> pass3 STAGING-LAST). Pass1 uses generate_room.py --lighting daylight (daylight_positive_template/daylight_negative, already in this file) instead of the firelit template. pass2_detail_populate_day is a lighting-neutral rewrite of the night pass2 (the night pass2 text explicitly says 'do not brighten the scene' / 'deepen the black voids', which fights a day-lit pass1 base — so day gets its own pass2 prompt_template but reuses the SAME rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots values, since the craft/de-clone/populate targets themselves are lighting-agnostic). pass3_staging_last_day applies the DAY staging law. Wired via generate_room.py --layered --day (implies --lighting daylight for pass1; routes pass2 to pass2_detail_populate_day + rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots, and pass3 to pass3_staging_last_day + rooms.<room>.layered_day.pass3_slots).

pass2_detail_populate_day._doc: Gemini instruction-edit detail/populate pass, DAY variant. Runs AFTER pass1 (daylit), on pass1's output asset. Same craft goals as the night pass2 but PRESERVES the bright daylit lighting instead of protecting dark chiaroscuro — reuses rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots (the same slot values as night; only the template text differs).

PRESERVE the exact composition, camera, room layout, and the bright DAYTIME lighting with its cool-neutral daylight key — do not darken the scene or add heavy chiaroscuro. IMPROVE only the craft: re-sculpt every {room_focal_features} so they read CRISPLY CHISELED with clean edge highlights; make every {room_repeat_elements} UNIQUE (remove cloned repeats); paint any flat gray or unfinished surfaces as weathered stone with clear daylit value modeling; add small environmental-storytelling clutter along walls and edges only ({room_clutter_vocab}) keeping the open floor areas clear. Keep the hand-painted oil-paint brushwork feel throughout. pass2_detail_populate_day.prompt_template_note: Reuses rooms.<room>.layered.pass2_slots (same slot values as the night pass2 — room_focal_features/room_repeat_elements/room_clutter_vocab are lighting-agnostic craft targets).

pass3_staging_last_day._doc: Gemini instruction-edit DAY STAGING pass. Runs LAST, on pass2's output asset (pass2 is the SAME detail/populate pass as night — see pipeline doc above). DAY STAGING LAW (owner spec, G5a): bright directional daylight through windows/doorways as the PRIMARY light; interior ambient lifted but still painterly (not flat/museum-lit); hearth/braziers/candles still lit but SECONDARY accents; long soft shadows cast by the window/doorway light; palette shifts cool-neutral daylight vs the night plates' warm firelight. Day plates will NOT meet the night staging-law luma bands (near-black %, hot-pool %, median-L target) — that is EXPECTED and recorded as data, not a FAIL.
pass3_staging_last_day.prompt_template: Edit this painterly isometric {room_setting_noun} plate. PRESERVE every detail exactly — the room layout, all {room_preserve_list} — change NOTHING about the content or composition. ONLY restage the LIGHTING into a DAYTIME scene: make {room_day_key_source} the dominant PRIMARY light source, bright directional daylight streaming through, with a cool-neutral daylight color temperature (not warm firelight). Lift the overall interior ambient so the room reads clearly and painterly (soft diffuse fill, NOT flat museum-lighting wash — keep gentle value modeling on every surface). Cast long SOFT directional shadows across the floor from the daylight direction. Keep {room_fill_source} still lit and glowing but now SECONDARY accents only, small warm pools that read as minor detail against the cool daylit scene, not the dominant light. The scene must read unmistakably as {room_space_desc} in daytime, keeping the hand-painted oil feel. Do NOT add any text, letters, numbers, runic writing that reads as text, labels, legends, map insets, UI elements, frames, or borders — the plate must contain ONLY the diegetic painted scene. Do NOT add any characters, people, figures, animals, or creatures of any kind — this is an EMPTY background plate; actors are composited in separately by the engine.
pass3_staging_last_day.prompt_template_note: slots: room_setting_noun, room_preserve_list (shared with night pass3), room_day_key_source (the daylight source noun phrase, e.g. 'the tall windows' daylight'), room_fill_source (shared with night pass3 — the secondary warm light, now demoted to accent), room_space_desc (shared with night pass3, day-appropriate phrasing implied by the prompt's own 'in daytime' clause).

registered_pipeline_2026_07_10._doc: ADOPTED pipeline for REGISTERED plates (PLATE SPRINT Phase 3 codification, 2026-07-10). Full rationale, evidence, and the REJECTED-APPROACHES list live in docs/roadmap/PLATE-RECIPE-DECISION.md (cross-linked from docs/research/2026-07-10-stage-tech-research.md and docs/RUNBOOK-INDEX.md) -- this block is the machine-readable params record, NOT a new default wiring: it does not change any room's canonical_plate/active pointer. Supersedes the implicit model_z-image img2img default as the RECORDED best-known recipe. WIRING STATUS (checked 2026-07-10, review finding on this PR): step 1 (base_pass, flux ControlNet depth) IS wired today via generate_room.py --controlnet depth. Step 2 (style_pass, Gemini instruction-edit with the structure/dimetric-lock clauses below) is NOT wired to a CLI flag yet -- generate_room.py --style-pass today runs the REJECTED ARM A two-stage model_z-image img2img pass (see the REJECTED-APPROACHES register), a different code path from the adopted Gemini step recorded here; do not conflate the two. Wiring a dedicated flag for the adopted Gemini style pass is a follow-up, not part of this PR.

base_pass._doc: Step 1: the greybox-registered base. Registration by construction -- the flux ControlNet depth pass locks paint to the authored geometry (see generate_room.py _resolve_controlnet / _build_base_pass_request, W6.3b #1470).
base_pass.source: the room greybox render (build_room_greybox.cs), NOT a painted reference

style_pass._doc: Step 2: the Gemini instruction-edit style pass over the registered base, carrying the STRUCTURE-LOCK and DIMETRIC-LOCK clauses below (verbatim source: qa/evidence/plate-sprint/camp-armB/style_pass_prompt_winning.txt for structure-lock, qa/evidence/plate-sprint/forest-road/forest_road_stylepass_prompt_dimetric.txt for dimetric-lock). THE REFERENCE-IMAGES LAW (see decision record): Gemini referenceImages hijack CONTENT toward the reference, not just style -- a reference is safe ONLY if its composition already matches the room greybox (e.g. an anchor minted FROM that same greybox). For rooms with no greybox-aligned anchor, use NO referenceImages -- text style description + scene-content grounding instead (no-ref reg 0.9439 vs same-room-ref 0.81-0.84, PR #1492).
style_pass.structure_lock_clause: CRITICAL STRUCTURE-LOCK (non-negotiable, checked pixel-by-pixel against the original): every wall, pillar, archway, doorway, staircase, tree, boulder, road edge, and prop must stay in EXACTLY its current position, size, and shape -- do NOT move, add, remove, resize, re-project, or recompose ANYTHING; only the paint and lighting treatment changes. Do NOT introduce any repeated, cloned, or tiled decorative motifs. Do NOT add any text, letters, numbers, labels, legends, map insets, UI elements, frames, or borders. Do NOT add any characters, people, figures, or creatures.
style_pass.dimetric_lock_clause: This is a TOP-DOWN DIMETRIC (2:1 isometric) game BACKGROUND PLATE viewed at a fixed ~30-degree downward camera pitch -- you are looking DOWN onto the scene from high above and to the side, exactly like a Pillars of Eternity II pre-rendered isometric level. Keep that EXACT high dimetric bird's-eye angle: there is NO horizon and NO sky band across the top of the frame -- the top of the frame is MORE ground/ceiling seen from above. Do NOT tilt the camera to an eye-level, first-person, or landscape-horizon view.
style_pass.reference_images_default: NONE unless the reference is an anchor minted FROM the same room's greybox (the crypt adoption's degenerate safe case)
